newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - Jan 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - Jan 27.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
- Premier Li Peng inspects Anshan Iron and Steel Company, a steel production giant empolying 500,000 people, 120,000 of whom are retirees.
- The All-China Journalists Association encourages public supervision over journalists. Several media groups banned paid services on January 23.
- Per capita income of Chinese farmers reached 1,900 yuan in 1996, up 20 percent from 1995 due in large part to good harvest.
- China corn output in 1996 was one fifth total world output. China seen producing 100 million tonnes each year.
- State Development Bank plans to offer 14.7 billion yuan in loans for first quarter of 1997.
- Rita Fan Hsu Lai-tai becomes president of the Provisional Legislative Council of Hong Kong.
- Number and quality of lawyers in China increasing; 60,000 more lawyers from 1993 and 4,500 more low firms from the same year.
- International and Commercial Bank of China's new governor Liu Tinghuan says to continue support to big and profitable state firms while banning loans to villas and hotels.
- Central bank survey finds 67 percent of Chinese holding foreign currency.
- Central bank governor Dai Xianglong praises foreign exchange officials for sound management of rising foreign exchange reserves and safeguarding better earnings.
- Foreign funded firms conduct 56 percent of Shanghai's foreign trade in 1996.
- China's supply and marketing cooperatives attract 2.0 billion yuan in foreign investment.
- China agricultural sector attracts 440 million yuan in foreign aid and investment in 1996.
